segments.text: Astrid is an extendable agent toolset, focused on the open-source AI art ecosystem.
It's built around two ideas.
One: giving agents tools and structures that make complex multimedia and AI work easy.
Two: giving agents reflective, creative, and technical knowledge of each system.
Going into the first: there's a lot of complexity to working with open-source models, and Astrid is built to live in that world.
Deep connectors let agents work on top of open-source tools.
For example, VibeComfy lets your agent deeply understand VibeComfy workflows and the ecosystem around them — and work within them.
Connectors to tools like AI Toolkit let it train new models, and it can additionally hook into any MCP server for more.

Second, for working with multimedia: we provide tools for agents to work with complex forms like video timelines — to understand them, and work with them in depth, using both image and video understanding models.
And third, there's a built-in data structure that automatically organizes all of your actions and all of your generations, and gives agents tools to work with them.
For each of these, we provide strong defaults.
You can customize them as you please. Everything is built to be a plugin.
The second is Hivemind — an open collection of messages and workflows from the community.
When you ask a query, it references and understands best practices from across the ecosystem, as well as guides others have added from their own experience.

While Hivemind already has thousands of workflows and a million-plus messages — and lots more right now — the goal is that your agents add to it as you discover things, as you learn best practices. It automatically adds to this repository that you just use and learn from.
So here's an example of all of this in action.
I wanted to make this exact video, and the first clip is a plant growing out of the soil in the desert.
I use Flux Kline to generate a lot of different samples and find ones I eventually like.
Then, for the hard shot, I use GPT Image — all of these, through built-in connectors.
Then I use Minimax to generate a bunch of different variants.
So I have this one that looks good, but then there's a weird glitch in it that I need to replace.
It finds the matching workflow for using masks with Minimax, and generates the fixed clip — even spinning up a RunPod instance, because my GPU is too slow for this.
Now that I have the first shot, I map out the rest — based on the timing of the music, it suggests transition points, and I work with it to get them perfect.
Then we work with the LLM to generate prompts for each of these segments — and I keep getting feedback on the overall trajectory of the video.
One more thing — Astrid works as a tool you use with other agents, like Codex, Claude, or Hermes. Or you can run it independently, all on its own.
If you want to try Astrid, give feedback, or join me in the Discord where I'm building this — you'll find instructions on GitHub and Discord. Links are below!
